events.title: The Critical Balance: Prompt vs. Context Window
events.subtitle: AI-Native Software Development — Only Builders Club
events.speaker: Vahid Faraji
events.description: Vahid breaks down the critical factors that determine the efficiency of AI assistants — context window vs. prompt distinction, token economics, cost management, and IDE planning with GitHub Copilot.
topics: Context Window vs. Prompt — the difference and token economics
Limits, cost management, and IDE planning (GitHub Copilot example)
Spec preparation, refactoring workflows with Numpy/Pandas code examples
takeaways: Understand the distinction between prompt and context window
Learn token economy fundamentals for cost-efficient AI usage
Practical spec preparation techniques for AI-assisted development
Refactoring strategies using real Numpy/Pandas code

events.title: AI-Native Software Development with Context Engineering
events.subtitle: Context Budget Visibility & Token Economics — SaaS Bridge
events.speaker: Vahid Faraji
events.description: Introduced Tokalator to SaaS developers — covering real-time token budget monitoring, tab relevance scoring, caching break-even economics, and the MCP server for Claude Code. Feedback session revealed demand for a standalone CLI and improved turn-count visibility.
topics: Real-time context budget monitoring inside VS Code
Tab relevance scoring — closing distractors automatically
Caching break-even analysis and conversation cost strategies
MCP server and CLI for Claude Code integration
takeaways: Understand which files silently consume your token budget
Use /optimize to remove distractor tabs and reclaim context
Calculate when prompt caching pays off (break-even at n*=2 turns)
Integrate Tokalator token counts into any MCP-capable agent
feedback: Requests for a standalone CLI for non-VS Code workflows (addressed by tokalator-mcp)
Improved turn-count visibility to show remaining turns within current budget
Minor UI bugs: tab count refresh delay on first load, edge case in relevance display

events.title: Context Engineering for AI-Native Development
events.subtitle: Token Budgets, Relevance Scoring & Developer Feedback — TechCareer Community
events.speaker: Vahid Faraji
events.description: Community session at TechCareer introducing Tokalator's context engineering approach to a broad developer audience. Covered token budget decomposition, the five-signal relevance scorer, and live demos of the VS Code extension and web calculators. Rich Q&A produced actionable feedback on CLI needs, turn tracking, and minor bugs.
topics: Context window vs. prompt — sources of invisible token consumption
Five-signal tab relevance scorer — how it ranks open files
Live demo: VS Code extension, /breakdown, /optimize commands
Web platform calculators — caching ROI, conversation cost, Cobb-Douglas optimizer
takeaways: Instruction files and config tabs are the largest hidden budget consumers
Context rot is measurable and addressable with the right tooling
Turn-based cost grows quadratically — conversation strategy selection matters
feedback: Strong interest in a standalone CLI for terminal-first workflows
Request for per-turn remaining-budget indicator inside the IDE
Several minor bugs reported: occasional stale token count in dashboard, edge case in multi-root workspace detection
